intro: Reykjavik is the northernmost capital on Earth, and in winter the sky itself is the main event.
facts: Start at Hallgrímskirkja, the rocket shaped church you can see from everywhere, and ride the tower lift for a view over the rainbow colored rooftops.
Walk the waterfront to the Sun Voyager, a steel Viking ship sculpture pointed at the sea, with snow capped Mount Esja across the bay.
Step inside Harpa, the concert hall wrapped in honeycomb glass that glows in different colors at night, and it is free to wander.
Eat a famous hot dog at the harbor stand that has fed the city since 1937, then warm up in a geothermal pool like the locals.
From September to April, drive twenty minutes out of the city lights, and on a clear night the northern lights can fill the entire sky.
outro: Save this for your Reykjavik trip.
